liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): Stranger into Franklin's Tower made a good opening to the show; Stranger opens the show, with Jerry's wah-wah adding energy after the structured section [11][21]
- **Cumberland Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Cumberland Blues rips; Reviewer likes Jerry's lead break in Cumberland Blues and enjoyed Stranger [14][16]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower is a strong, compelling eight-minute version [21]
- US Blues ended the first set as a nice surprise after Let It Grow [11]
- US Blues was a surprise in the setlist, with Cumberland Blues a highlight of the second set [13]
- Dupree's, Let It Grow and US Blues made a great closing sequence for set one [17]
- Jerry going into US Blues to close the tight first set surprised the crowd [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-04-05 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t02 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t03 Franklin's Tower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t04 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t05 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t06 Memphis Blues Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t07 Far From Me**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-05 t08 Dupree's Diamond Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-05.141802.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 166 min [1]
- **gd1989-04-05.145037.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1989-04-05.144913.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 19 songs; 164 min [3]
- **gd1989-04-05.aud.bleich.sirmick.83800.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 161 min [4]. Said about its sound: Tape flips in the Drums to Space transition and the Not Fade Away chant were crossfaded [4]
- **gd89-04-05.sbd-matrix.unknown.5491.sbefail.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4.11/5 by 9 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this recording sounds pretty good [20]
- **gd89-04-05.sbd-matrix.kowalski.1091.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 153 min; rated 3.84/5 by 19 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound excellent, rating it four stars [13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer had front-row, seat 1 tickets via mail order; the week also included a basketball national championship and Hash Bash on campus [10]
- Ann Arbor had just won the NCAA title and fans partied hard; the small venue's main floor was about 20 rows [18]
- Phil played a new bass that looked striking; the reviewer sat stage left [18]
- Reviewer notes the band rarely spent two nights in Ann Arbor, or more than one night in Michigan [21]
- Show is short, especially the second set, which is a standard list for the era with no real jamming [11]
- Clean 1989 versions of most songs, but no intense jamming; the show fades after Stranger > Franklin's [13]
- First half of set two lacked the usual open jams, but the songs were well played and Cumberland fit [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-05.141802.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck, Sony ESX-HiFi/L750 tape); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS); Transfer Info: Master PCM… [1]. Also: Recorded with Schoeps CMC4/MK4 microphones, as the file name indicates [1]
- **gd1989-04-05.145037.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]. Also: Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics to PCM by Ted Mattes, covering very short tape flips; 16-bit 44.1 files [2]
- **gd1989-04-05.144913.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [3]. Also: Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics to PCM by Ted Mattes, covering very short tape flips; 24-bit release [3]
- **gd1989-04-05.aud.bleich.sirmick.83800.sbeok.flac16**: taped by John Bleich; transferred by SirMick; source: aud > Nak 300 shotguns > WMD-6 > mac [4]. Also: Audience recording from tapes lent by John; mastered with iZotope Ozone and TC Works Native Dex; Discs 2 and 3 are joined seamlessly [4]
- **gd89-04-05.sbd-matrix.unknown.5491.sbefail.shnf**: source: Healy Ultra Mix Cassette Master-> DAT-> CDR [6]
- **gd89-04-05.sbd-matrix.kowalski.1091.sbeok.shnf**: source: Healy Ultra Mix - sbd+aud> cm> dat> cd [7]
